recipes.name: Spicy Chicken and Sweet Potato Stew
ingredients_raw: 1 pound sweet potato, peeled and cubed
1 orange bell pepper, seeded and cubed
1 (16 ounce) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Stir in onion and garlic; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in sweet potato, bell pepper, chicken, tomatoes, and 2 cups of water. Season with salt, chili powder, cumin, oregano, cocoa powder, cinnamon, and red pepper flakes. Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a boil. Dissolve flour in 2 tablespoons water, and stir in to boiling stew. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the potatoes are tender but not mushy, 10 to 20 minutes. Stir the stew occasionally to keep it from sticking.
Once the potatoes are done, stir in corn and kidney beans. Cook a few minutes until hot, then stir in cilantro before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Chicken and Sweet Potato Stew
raw_recipe.description: With flavors reminiscent of Morocco and Mexico, this easy yet richly-flavored spicy chicken and sweet potato stew contains loads of chicken, vegetables, and some surprising spices.

review.reviewBody: For CROCK POT: Saute onions, garlic & bell pepper in oil (+ add ~TBSP butter). After cooking ~5 minutes, stir in flour. Slowly add water while stirring till smooth. Transfer to crock pot. Add remaining ingredients. NOTE: I cut raw chicken breast into about three chunks each and added to crock pot (raw). Toward the end of cooking, I shredded the chicken with fork to make it more of a stew consistancy.

Delicious! Very versatile as far as ingredients go. I've made this a number of times now, using either vegetable or chicken broth, rather than the 2 cups of water, depending on what I have on hand. I have used various colours of peppers, such as red, orange, yellow mix. A bit of green if I've got some to use up, and Cornstarch rather than flour to thicken sauce. Black turtle beans if that's what I have instead of or addition with kidney beans. I do add some additional chicken, i.e 1.5 lbs ( rather than 1 lb) cubed chicken breast, and cook the raw chicken in the pot after onion and garlic are about halfway done. Have shared some as a 'meal train'/ gift of a quick reheat meal! Everyone loves it. Bachelor, elderly, friends hint that they'd like it again when I make it. I typically make a double batch. This Freezes well, as long as you portion some out to freeze BEFORE the Sweet Potatoes are fully cooked. (about halfway- 3/4 way at most- so they aren't mushy on defrost/ reheat. Defrost it and it reheats well, so make a double batch! (in a dutch oven- stovetop- or adapt to the crock pot recipe another person noted in comments, if that works better for you. Use Freezer bags for portioning for freezer/future easy meal and freezer storage; give a meal to a friend or neighbour who could use one! Serve (or give some away) with crusty bread or rolls, or warmed, toasted Tortillas/ Tortilla chips at the table, and dinner is served! YUM.

This was way so good. The only changes I made were a few squirts of lime juice and I messed up and thawed two pieces of white fish that I thought was chicken breasts. I cooked the fish in the air fryer and dumped it into the stew instead of chicken. Awesome. Served over rice. Spices were terrific and I am not a fan of hot spicy foods.

This was family approved!!! I doubled the liquid - not water, I used chicken broth, and I used black beans instead of kidney beans because my husband doesn’t like kidney beans. And since I doubled the liquid, I left the lid off at the end. And I probably tripled the red pepper flakes!

Made this in the slow cooker, left out the green pepper, the flour and used chicken broth in place of water. I replaced the kidney beans with black beans and added green beans about 2 hours before serving.

Fantastic. Converted to slow cooker and doubled recipe. Used chicken thighs, cubed and slightly browned before putting in pot. Cut sweet potato in small chunks. Put everything in slow cooker, except chicken, cooked on high for total of 6 hours. Put chicken in about half way through. Didn't have any cinnamon so used 2 cinnamon sticks - fabulous aroma. Great melding of flavors. Will definitely make again. A real hit.

DELICIOUS! my husband and I LOVED this recipe! I used the crock-pot for 3-hrs on high, I sauteed the onions, garlic and peppers and coated them with flour and water before I put it in the crock-pot with chicken(raw) and the other ingredients. I went light on the chili powder. I'm trying a bunch of new stews to add to my menu and this will definitely be a favorite! Yumm!!!

Turned out better than expected! I made a few changes such as boiling the chicken and shredding it and then using that broth as my "2 cups of water". Shredding the chicken ensured me and my family a bit of chicken with every bite. I did what some comments have suggested such as adding Chayenne pepper for a little kick, because we too love things spicy. I also added a small can of tomato sauce and diced fresh tomatoes and carrots. I opted out of the corn or beans mainly because I didn't have any on hand. The spices are what really surprised me and worked out really well together in this dish. I had to add more spices to what seemed fit to my tasting. When topped it with fresh cilantro, the flavors came together beautifully. I would definitely make this again!

I made this in a crock pot with the following variations: Instead of flour, I used two tbsps of tomato paste as a thickener. I used paprika instead of chili powder. I don't digest kidney beans or corn well so I added green beans instead. I also added chopped chorizo sausage. Hmmmmm. Try your own variations. It took about 4 hours to cook on high. You could cook it on low for 8 or 9 hours and it would be ready to enjoy after a day's work.

FANTASTIC stew! A KEEPER! I used what I had: plum tomatoes that were getting soft, so used those w/ a 14 oz can of diced tomatoes. Also, had chicken thighs thawed, so browned them along w/ onion, pepper, garlic & spices b/f adding liquid (careful they don't burn!). The TASTE, AROMA & VISUAL APPEAL are great! I wouldn't change a thing in this recipe! Thanks RCKim!

Easy Version! Saute onion and garlic, add chicken stock (instead of water) raw diced chicken (breast or thigh), spices, red or orange pepper and drained tomatoes. Cook 10 minutes. Add diced sweet potato. Cook 10 minutes. Add flour slurry, beans (I used black beans since that was what I had on hand)and corn (though I left that out). Heat to boiling. Top with cilantro, squeeze of lime and dollop of sour cream (important!). Absolutely wonderful and very easy! Also, I substituted 1/4 square of unsweetened bakers chocolate since I didn't have cocoa on hand. Very forgiving recipe. Thank you!
For Arkansas folk, maybe a tad spicy. Sister in law will not eat it. I loved it. Perfect Heat. Easily can drop 1 T chili powder and red pepper flakes. I cooked the dish per recipe. Love it.
Very tasty and easy to put together! I used other reviewers suggestions to sub black beans for kidney beans and tomato paste for flour slurry. Everyone in my house ate it up!

This is definitely a keeper! I made it for a luncheon with a friend and we both had two bowls of it. I made two slight changes: I used one cup of chicken broth and one cup of water and I used a can of black beans (drained and rinsed) in place of the kidney beans because kidney beans are not a favorite of mine.
I didn't change a thing. It was delicious! Love the sweetness of the potatoes and corn with the spices!

I was not feeling energetic enough to add the chicken, hence only cut up one large sweet potato, used water as the recipe indicated, and did not have fresh cilantro on hand, so used dried cilantro spice. Also used whole wheat flour. Put it over some risotto and added a dollop of plain greek yogurt to temper the heat and.....YUMMMMMY! Thanks for the recipe!
I thought this was fabulous. I added more chicken (and used thighs) and a little bit less sweet potato.
